title: Minimal unitary representations of time-invariant causal quantum channels
abstract: In this work, we study quantum channels that respect causality in single-input-single-output linear time-invariant systems. We show that positive semidefinite kernels satisfying certain analyticity constraints, which we call Schur-class kernels, provide a suitable description of such channels through multiplicative maps (Schur multipliers). Using the Moore-Aronszajn Theorem, we establish that these multipliers admit a minimal analytic Stinespring representation, which, in the unital case, is given by multiplication by a left inner function. We then relate the output rank of pure-state inputs to the dimension of the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Using de Branges-Rovnyak realizations, we derive a stability criterion for the existence of two-sided inner completions of these vector-valued functions. We further show that the adjoint of the Julia embedding associated with the realization is minimal, and that its characteristic function essentially coincides with the canonical two-sided inner completion suggested by the Beurling-Lax-Halmos Theorem. Finally, we provide algorithms for explicitly computing minimal two-sided inner completions in the case of finite McMillan degree.
summary: This paper provides a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing causal quantum channels in LTI systems. It shows that these channels are characterized by specific positive semidefinite kernels (Schur-class kernels). The core result links the physical requirement of unitary implementation to a deep mathematical property: the existence of a two-sided inner completion for the associated function, providing both a criterion and explicit algorithms for computation.
main_problem: The paper studies the mathematical characterization of quantum channels that respect causality in single-input-single-output linear time-invariant (LTI) quantum systems.
main_result: It establishes that the existence of a unitary implementation for such a channel is equivalent to the associated Schur-class kernel admitting a minimal two-sided inner completion.
method: The analysis heavily employs advanced functional analysis, including Schur-class kernels, de Branges-Rovnyak realization theory, and techniques from Hardy space theory.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum channel $\Phi: T(\mathcal{H}_A) 	o T(\mathcal{H}_B)$ acting on trace-class operators, analyzed in the context of time-invariant, causal systems.
key_observables: Output rank of pure-state inputs, the characteristic function of the associated embedding, and the existence of two-sided inner completions.
important_parameters: Causality (analyticity in the upper half-plane), Unitality ($\Phi^*[I] = I$), and the McMillan degree (for explicit algorithms).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be modeled by positive semidefinite kernels (Schur-class kernels) and relies on the structure provided by the Moore-Aronszajn and de Branges-Rovnyak theorems.
figures_summary: Not specified (The notes detail mathematical algorithms and theoretical results rather than figure descriptions).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem (causal quantum channels) to mapping it onto mathematical structures (Schur-class kernels/multipliers). It then uses advanced function theory (Hardy spaces, RKHS) to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for unitary implementation, culminating in explicit computational algorithms.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical tools to analyze physical constraints (like causality) on quantum operations, which is crucial for designing realistic quantum communication protocols or characterizing open quantum systems.
